wheat___Stripe_rust.cause: Fungus (Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici), also called yellow rust
symptoms: Small pale spots appear first on the leaves.
Yellow to light orange pustules break out of the spots.
After tillering, the pustules line up along the leaf veins, giving the leaf a striped look.
In severe cases pustules also develop on the heads.
treatment: On susceptible varieties, consider a fungicide when stripe rust has been found in the region and cool, wet weather is forecast.
Spraying at flag leaf emergence protects the flag leaf and reduces yield loss.
Fungicides work best before the disease is well developed; spraying after it has taken hold is unlikely to give good control.
Protection lasts about 21 to 28 days and does not cover new growth, so a second spray may be needed.
prevention: Plant resistant varieties: this is the main way to manage stripe rust.
Avoid a variety the next season if it had significant stripe rust in your area.
Do not plant winter wheat too early.
Control grassy weeds and volunteer wheat.
wheat___Stripe_rust.severity: Develops best at 50 to 64 °F. Currently the most economically important wheat rust, with yield losses reaching 100% in susceptible varieties.

sources.title: An Overview of Stripe Rust of Wheat, Crop Protection Network
A review of wheat diseases: a field perspective, Molecular Plant Pathology

wheat___Septoria_leaf_blotch.cause: Fungus (Zymoseptoria tritici), also called septoria tritici blotch
symptoms: Elongated oval spots form on leaves; they are limited by the leaf veins, so they look rectangular.
Water-soaked patches appear, surrounded by yellowing or dead leaf tissue.
Spots merge into large areas of dead brown tissue.
Mature spots may contain small black dots, but these are not always visible.
treatment: Fungicides are the main control in most crops.
Time sprays to protect the lower leaves first and then the upper leaves.
Use a balanced fungicide mix to slow resistance.
prevention: Grow varieties with high septoria resistance ratings.
Avoid sowing early: later autumn sowing lowers disease pressure.
wheat___Septoria_leaf_blotch.severity: Losses of 50% may occur in severely affected crops.

sources.title: Septoria tritici in winter wheat, AHDB
A review of wheat diseases: a field perspective, Molecular Plant Pathology
